the momentum distributions of parton constituents of the nucleon and the nuclear dependence of these distributions.
the momentum distribution of quarks inside the nucleons.
the momentum and coordinate space distributions of quarks and gluons in the nucleon, and the nuclear effects on these distributions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quark momentum distributions in the nucleon are not very sensitive to the nuclear size, and that the nuclear effects observed in deep inelastic scattering are due to large distance shadowing, which is a phenomenon that is not directly related to the parton momentum distributions.
nuclear effects in the momentum distributions of parton distributions are very small, but that the shadowing effects at large distances are large.

the nuclear dependence of structure functions is dominated by the shadowing of partonic degrees of freedom at distances larger than 2.5fm, but that the small nuclear dependence observed at shorter distances is a reflection of a small nuclear dependence of quark distributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quark distributions in the nucleons are not significantly modified by the presence of other nucleons.
the quark momentum distributions are not very much changed in nuclei, while the parton shadowing in nuclei is large and is due to shadowing of the nucleon structure functions.
the momentum distributions in the nucleon are largely independent of nuclear size, and that shadowing effects are dominated by the long-range correlations in nuclear matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nuclear dependence of the structure functions can be understood in terms of the momentum distributions of parton in nuclei.
the nuclear dependence of the structure function can be used to study the quark dynamics inside the nucleon, and the nuclear dependence of quark dynamics is small for t ≲ 2 fm.
